learningObjectives: Distinguish local workspaces from their repository type.
Explain ordinary checkout and administrative revocation.
Exchange subsets with dependency, rights and synchronization limits.
Apply an independent peer-review process and prepare an authorized local browser target.

elements.text: Commander organizes models, TestCases, execution objects and requirements in workspace tabs. This guide focuses on those areas without claiming a fixed total number of sections. Modules are reusable models, not exclusively UI models.

The project tree shows object hierarchy; Details supports editing the selected object. Open sections from Home → Section. To compare tabs side by side, drag a tab onto the docking element. Do not assume the historical New Vertical Tab Group label exists in every release.

Save stores project changes; Undo/Redo and navigation shortcuts are separate functions. Independent guidance: inspect the available undo and recovery commands for your version and context rather than assuming Save permanently disables every recovery method.

elements.text: Single-user workspaces have a local database for individual work. Multi-user collaboration uses a separate workspace per user and machine, connected to a common repository. A local workspace path alone does not determine the repository type or prove who can access its files.

Checkout reserves an object for editing; another ordinary user cannot edit that checked-out object. Checkin publishes changes and frees objects. Checkout updates the selected objects; use Update all for unrelated repository changes.

Administrators can revoke checkouts in the primary repository, rejecting the holder’s unpublished changes and new objects. This is not a simultaneous merge or ordinary tester lock override. Coordinate with the owner before administrative recovery.

elements.text: Export Subset packages selected objects and linked dependencies; authorized users can import it into another repository. Import does not keep the two copies synchronized. Project-root definitions and ViewingGroupName/OwningGroupName access rights are not exported; review destination configuration and rights.
Import targets the project root or a ComponentFolder; multi-user checkout applies. Inspect duplicate-Module import/merge decisions rather than treating import as an unrestricted copy.
The Standard subset includes ready-made Modules. A version migration does not automatically add every new Standard subset Module; import the applicable release subset and inspect affected tests.

Independent guidance: use descriptive names and separate shared resources from project-specific artifacts. A possible structure has templates/references, reusable cross-project resources and one folder per project. This is an example, not a mandatory three-folder repository rule certified from the gated Academy video.

Independent peer-review workflow: a tester moves work from In Work to Ready for Approval; a second reviewer records approval or returns changes. These labels illustrate your team process; they are not a universal built-in Tosca enforcement or an unskippable product state machine.

elements.text: Create a disposable single-user workspace and inspect its repository type. Identify models, TestCases and execution areas; arrange two tabs using docking. Academy Exercise 01 was inaccessible, so this is independent practice guidance and no Commander execution was performed.

For local Chrome XBrowser/XScan automation, prepare the Tricentis Automation Extension in the actual target browser. This does not claim every supported remote or alternative-engine workflow uses the same setup.

Independent guidance: explore an authorized disposable application, document the intended flow and expected results, then identify controls to model. Manual exploration helps understanding but does not guarantee complete coverage.

Choose an authorized sandbox with suitable test data, map a reversible user journey and its expected outcome. Academy Exercise 02 and its original target were inaccessible; no original course completion or live application execution is certified.

examPitfalls.title: Inferring repository type from a path
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming every local workspace is single-user.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Check the repository type; multi-user testers also have local workspaces.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming imported copies synchronize
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Expecting destination edits to update the export source.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Review dependencies and destination rights explicitly.

examPitfalls.title: Treating a historical menu label as universal
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming one tab-group label exists in every release.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use documented docking for the current interface.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing team process and product enforcement
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating the example review labels as unavoidable built-in states.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Agree and enforce your organization’s process.

examPitfalls.title: Overgeneralizing browser setup
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Applying local Chrome prerequisites to every engine.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Check the specific engine and target environment.

examPitfalls.title: Treating Save as universal loss of recovery
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming no recovery command can ever apply after saving.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect undo settings, local/repository state and relevant recovery commands.

examPitfalls.title: Denying administrator recovery
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Claiming only the checkout holder can release any lock.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Ordinary editing is exclusive; primary-repository administrators can revoke and reject unpublished changes.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester explicitly created a single-user workspace. How should a colleague collaborate on the same shared test assets?

options.text: Assume a two-user editing limit.
Assume the workspace already uses a common repository.
Grant an OS admin role and assume shared-repository collaboration exists.
Prepare a multi-user repository and separate user workspaces; the single-user workspace is for individual work.

practiceQuiz.rationale: Single-user storage is not the shared-repository collaboration model.

optionExplanations.A: No two-user limit defines this type.
optionExplanations.C: An OS role does not create the collaboration infrastructure.
optionExplanations.D: This uses the documented team workspace model.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How can authorized users exchange selected Modules and TestCases between separate repositories?

options.text: Export a subset and import it into the destination, reviewing dependencies and rights.
Copy a multi-user workspace folder and assume its identity is safe.
Subsets can never cross repositories.
Assume a shared repository publishes to every separate repository automatically.

practiceQuiz.rationale: Subset export/import transfers objects; it does not synchronize repositories.

optionExplanations.A: This is the supported exchange workflow.
optionExplanations.B: Direct copying is not artifact exchange and can break multi-user identity.
optionExplanations.D: Separate repositories do not automatically share changes.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which documented operation displays Commander tabs side by side?

options.text: Open arbitrary duplicate application instances.
Drag a tab onto the desired docking position.
Assume a universal split-screen menu without checking the release.
Tabs cannot be arranged.

practiceQuiz.rationale: Docking changes where tab content is displayed.

optionExplanations.A: This does not use the documented arrangement operation.
optionExplanations.C: The claimed menu is not established.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In this independent team workflow, which status signals completed work awaiting peer approval?

options.text: Approved/Completed
In Work
Ready for Approval
A universal product-required Under Review state

practiceQuiz.rationale: The example separates tester readiness from reviewer approval.

optionExplanations.A: Approval belongs to the reviewer after evaluation.
optionExplanations.B: This describes active work in the example.
optionExplanations.C: This signals readiness in the defined workflow.
optionExplanations.D: No universal built-in state requirement is established.

practiceQuiz.scenario: For local Chrome automation through XBrowser/XScan, which browser preparation is documented?

options.text: Assume no extension is needed.
Use any unrelated scraping extension.
Replace XBrowser with an assumed Selenium plugin.
Install and enable the Tricentis Automation Extension in the target Chrome browser.

practiceQuiz.hint: The question specifies the engine and browser.
practiceQuiz.rationale: This is the documented local browser prerequisite.

optionExplanations.A: The stated engine needs its extension.
optionExplanations.B: An unrelated extension does not configure XBrowser.
optionExplanations.C: This is not the stated engine’s extension.
optionExplanations.D: This prepares the intended local browser.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which THREE practices suit the independent team organization example in this lesson?

options.text: Consistent descriptive naming.
Separate reusable resources and project-specific artifacts.
A second person reviews work before team approval.
Put every artifact at the root with no ownership or structure.

practiceQuiz.hint: These are independent team practices, not mandatory product states.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Naming, deliberate organization and peer review support maintainability.

optionExplanations.B: This separates reuse and project ownership.
optionExplanations.C: A separate reviewer provides another check.
optionExplanations.D: An unstructured root obscures ownership and reuse.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does the Standard subset provide for common supported operations?

options.text: Ready-made Standard Modules.
The source code of every application.
Automatic user access to all repositories.
Guaranteed successful execution reports without tests.

practiceQuiz.hint: Reusable tools are not application correctness.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The subset supplies reusable Modules, which still need appropriate configuration.

optionExplanations.A: This is the reusable toolkit role.
optionExplanations.B: It does not package every SUT’s source code.
optionExplanations.C: Modules do not grant repository access.
optionExplanations.D: A toolkit does not prove execution outcomes.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which folder categories describe the independent example in this lesson?

options.text: Design | Development | Production
Templates/references | Reusable cross-project resources | Per-project artifacts
Only a fixed global set of exactly three product sections
Draft | In Review | Approved are mandatory storage types

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish example organization from product enforcement.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The example separates templates, reuse and project ownership without mandating exactly three folders.

optionExplanations.A: These are lifecycle/environment labels, not this example.
optionExplanations.C: No exhaustive section count is claimed.
optionExplanations.D: Workflow labels are not mandatory storage types.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Tester A has checked out a Module. What happens when ordinary Tester B tries to modify it, without administrative recovery?

options.text: Tester B’s ordinary rights bypass checkout.
Both edit and automatically merge.
The checked-out object cannot be modified by B until it is released.
It is locked only if A sets a separate Read-Only property.

practiceQuiz.rationale: Checkout prevents another ordinary editor changing the reserved object; administrators have a separate primary-repository revocation mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: Ordinary editing does not bypass checkout.
optionExplanations.C: This states the ordinary lock behavior.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After saving, a tester finds a mistake. Which recovery approach is responsible?

options.text: Assume Ctrl+Z always reverses any saved repository change.
Reopen and assume saved changes disappear.
Assume a File → Revert command restores every prior state.
Inspect available undo/recovery commands and local/repository state; correct the intended change or use an appropriate reviewed recovery.

practiceQuiz.rationale: Do not promise unlimited undo or claim saving disables every recovery method.

optionExplanations.A: Undo availability does not guarantee this result.
optionExplanations.B: Reopening does not discard saved data automatically.
optionExplanations.C: The asserted universal command is unsupported.
optionExplanations.D: This investigates applicable recovery instead of guessing.

quickRecap.value: Separate local workspaces connected to a common repository.
Exchange artifacts; imported copies do not synchronize.
Independent team workflow, not universal enforced states.
Arrange tabs using the docking element.
Separate templates, reusable resources and project artifacts as appropriate.
Prepare the stated engine’s actual browser environment.
Inspect local/repository state and applicable commands.
